summary: One script-rendered form at /login/ on the connection's own origin: the account (code, CPF, CNPJ or domain) and the password together, then a Continue button. The site may then ask for a Cloudflare Turnstile check, and accounts with two-factor authentication are asked for an authenticator code, a security key or a recovery code.

sources.title: Registro.br's own sign-in form component, as the site serves it: the compiled Vue module LoginForm
sources.note: The page at /login/ is an empty script shell; this module builds its sign-in form. It passes the ids login.user and login.password, the autocomplete values username and current-password and the type password to the site's field component, and renders a button with the classes bt and bt-next that reads the form before sign-in.

sources.title: Registro.br's own field component, as the site serves it: the compiled Vue module AppField
sources.note: Renders an input element whose id and name are both the id it is given, with the given type (text when none) and autocomplete. A disabled field is rendered read-only.

sources.title: Registro.br: contract for registering a domain under .br (version of 26 November 2024), the site's only terms document
sources.note: Read from the site's own module DomainContract. It binds the holder to keep the password secret and has no clause on automated access to the site.

selectors.note: The id comes from the form module and the name from the field component, which gives every input its id as its name.

The Continue button. It is disabled until the fields are valid, and its own handler checks with the site before signing in; it is replaced by an Access button while a check or a second factor is shown.

fixtures.note: Built from the two compiled modules; nothing was rendered. Labels, texts and styles are left out.

staysInteractive.note: The site can require a Cloudflare Turnstile check before the password is sent; the form then shows it and an Access button.
An account with an authenticator token is asked for its six-digit code in the same form (field id login.totp). No authenticator challenge is written: the field was read from code, not observed.
An account with a registered security key is asked to use it.
Recovery codes, the eight-digit access key and the password reminder.

unverified: The page can change at any time; the module names carry a build hash that changes with each release.
The rendered page was not observed: every selector is worked out from compiled code, not seen in a page.
That the Continue button becomes enabled when the application types into the two fields.
When the site remembers the last account, it fills the account field itself; whether that stops automatic sign-in was not established.
Nothing after the Continue button was observed, because no account was used.
neededFromUser: The sign-in page saved from the user's own browser as "Webpage, Complete" and read with the capture tool's --from-file mode. The site is script-rendered, so the saved file must hold the rendered page, not the empty shell. Save any page signed out and with no password typed in; keep the "_files" folder beside the .html and both outside the repository: they can hold the account name.
notes: Checked before reading, on the review date: robots.txt of registro.br is readable and none of its rules covers /login/ or /assets/; the only terms document, the registration contract, has no clause on automated access. Only the public script modules were read, with no rendering, no input and no request to the sign-in service. The 2026-10-12 review had not found the terms because they are rendered by script.
